title: Shell
subtitle: CLI between you and the kernel — flip for meaning, example, and notes

cards.meaning: Program that interprets commands and asks the kernel to do the real work
Bourne Shell — original Unix shell; many scripts still use #!/bin/sh
cards.notes: On modern Linux often a symlink to bash or dash (POSIX mode)

cards.meaning: GNU Bourne-Again Shell — default interactive shell on most Linux distros
C Shell — syntax looks more like C; less common on servers today
cards.notes: Only csh uses % for a normal-user prompt

cards.meaning: Korn Shell — Bourne-compatible with extra features; still seen on some Unix
Default prompt for a regular (non-root) user
Default root (superuser) prompt — commands can change the whole system
cards.notes: Hash = extra power; same across shells

cards.meaning: Shows the login shell from your account (passwd / SHELL var)
Name of the current shell process
cards.notes: A leading - often means login shell

cards.meaning: Stores your login shell (last field on your user line)
cards.notes: Not always the same as the shell of your current process ($0)
